Combat is really fun, the bosses are great and it's really well optimized(the fact that I can lock it to 90fps on a laptop GPU at high settings is pretty insane in 2026), it's one of the best souls-like game to come out in recent years. The game really allows you to experiment with combat and allows resetting skills so easily and has no associated cost (that I saw). I loved Sekiro so the parrying here is really fun with a enough ways to counter attack which make it really satisfying when you pull it off. The aspect I liked most about the combat is how fluid and responsive it is which is something we dont see often with such games. If you like fun, resposive combat and good boss battles with a pretty good amount of content it is a blind buy especially on a sale.

Cannot treat this game seriously due to how bad the camera is.

Looking around is buttery smooth, but walking makes the entire screen vibrate, because the camera is directly attached to an entity that updates less frequently than the game renders frames.

Developers tried, but failed to implement a proper fix, leaving only the "Smooth Camera" option that clumsily lerps camera position making everything blurry and for some unknown reason also ties the mouse movement to the FPS... like what, why?

Balatro is a game revolving around poker hands and a deck of cards you can improve and change throughout a run of the game. There is plenty of replayability in this game. tons of things to unlock, new challenges to complete, and new builds you can make. Balatro is a very relaxing cozy type beat, and fits that theme very well.

    It's a game that takes poker and makes it a rougelike deckbuilder, with the goal of beating the set of  required points to move onto the next set of required points. For someone who likes cards and poker... and rougelikes, this game caters to me. If you are someone who likes all three of those things, there is not a better way (that I have came across) to combine them in a game.

It's alright.
Pros:
combat is fun
exploration and puzzles are good
cute characters, some of the backstories almost made me cry

cons:
worldbuilding is barebones, the world feels too empty for what it's supposed to be
some of the in-game optional challenges are easy but annoying
sometimes it was unclear which path would take you forward and which would lead you to a side path. I was trying to do all of the side paths first, and sometimes got locked out.
The story ultimately didn't really go anywhere
Combat would quickly get trivially easy
The in-game hint system sucks and keeps giving hints for things you already know are there but can't get because you don't have the right items/abilities yet.

Overall I would still recommend it. Just be aware, if you have played similar games before, put the difficulty to max.

Edit: I should mention that the combat music makes me want to poop.
